_note: Country summaries for the EU map. Drafted Oct 2026 from public sources for policy-team review. Keep to facts that change rarely; no fee rates.

at.summary: Packaging must be licensed with an approved collection and recovery system, and household and commercial packaging are handled separately. Austria introduced a deposit on single-use drinks bottles and cans in 2025.
at.law: Packaging Ordinance 2014 (VVO), under the Waste Management Act
at.route: Licence with a collection system, e.g. ARA
at.note: Foreign distance sellers need an authorised representative in Austria.

be.summary: Belgium runs one packaging regime across its three regions, overseen by a single interregional commission. Household and industrial packaging are covered by separate schemes.
be.note: Companies placing more than 300 kg of packaging a year must report.

bg.summary: Producers either join a licensed recovery organisation or pay product fees themselves. Registration is with the Executive Environment Agency.
bg.law: Waste Management Act and Packaging Ordinance
bg.note: Producers outside a collective scheme pay product fees to the environmental fund (PUDOOS).

hr.summary: Croatia's packaging system is run centrally by the national Environmental Protection and Energy Efficiency Fund, which collects fees and reports. A digital producer register replaced paper filings in 2025.
hr.law: Ordinance on packaging and single-use plastic products (2023)
hr.route: Register and pay fees to the Fund
hr.note: Single-use drinks containers also carry a refund (deposit) fee.

cy.summary: Producers meet their packaging obligations through a licensed collective system or an approved individual system.
cy.route: Collective system, e.g. Green Dot Cyprus
cy.note: Applies to packaging placed on the Cypriot market, including imports.

cz.summary: Most producers transfer their take-back and recovery obligations to an authorised packaging company and report annually.
cz.note: Annual reporting covers packaging placed on the Czech market by material.

dk.summary: Denmark's packaging EPR has been in operation since 1 October 2025. Producers register, report household and commercial packaging separately, and most comply through a producer responsibility organisation.
dk.law: Executive Order No. 1146 of 2025 on packaging
dk.route: Join one of the approved PROs
dk.note: Fees on reports from October 2025 are environmentally graded.

ee.summary: Producers must transfer their obligations to a producer responsibility organisation by contract, or run their own system and pay packaging excise.
ee.route: PRO, e.g. Eesti Pakendiringlus or TVO
ee.note: Foreign producers register through an authorised representative in Estonia.

fi.summary: Packers and importers above the turnover threshold must join a producer organisation that runs collection and recycling.
fi.law: Waste Act and Government Decree on packaging
fi.note: Drinks containers are covered by the separate Palpa deposit system.

fr.summary: Producers must join an approved eco-organisation and obtain a unique identification number, which must appear on their terms of sale. Consumer packaging needs sorting information.
fr.law: Environmental Code, as amended by the AGEC law (2020)
fr.route: Eco-organisation, e.g. Citeo, Léko or Adelphe
fr.note: Triman logo and Info-tri sorting labels apply to household packaging.

de.summary: Every producer of packaging that ends up with private final consumers must register in LUCID and license it with a dual system before sale.
de.route: System participation with a dual system
de.note: Online marketplaces must check that their sellers are registered.

gr.summary: Registration applies from the first unit of packaging placed on the market, and producers usually join a licensed PRO.
gr.register: National Register of Producers (EM-PA), run by EOAN
gr.note: There is no de minimis threshold for registration.

hu.summary: Since July 2023 a state concession operator, MOHU, runs packaging waste management. Producers register and pay EPR fees quarterly.
hu.route: Quarterly declarations and fees to MOHU
hu.note: The separate environmental product charge is handled by the tax authority (NAV).

ie.summary: Larger producers must join an approved compliance scheme or self-comply and register with their local authority.
ie.register: Repak, or the local authority for self-compliers
ie.note: A deposit return scheme (Re-turn) has run for drinks containers since 2024.

it.summary: Producers and users of packaging join the national consortium CONAI and pay the environmental contribution on packaging they place on the market.
it.note: Packaging must carry environmental labelling for consumers.

lv.summary: Packers either pay natural resources tax on their packaging or join a licensed waste management system and are exempted.
lv.law: Packaging Law and Natural Resources Tax Law
lv.route: Licensed system, e.g. Latvijas Zaļais punkts
lv.note: Drinks containers are covered by a deposit return system.

lt.summary: All packaging producers and importers must register and keep records in GPAIS, even when a producer organisation handles their compliance.
lt.law: Law on Packaging and Packaging Waste Management
lt.route: Producer organisation, or pay pollution tax
lt.note: Drinks containers are covered by a deposit system.

lu.summary: Household packaging obligations are usually met through the approved organisation Valorlux, with oversight from the Environment Agency.
lu.note: Producers can apply for an individual approval instead.

mt.summary: Producers join an authorised compliance scheme that collects and recovers packaging waste on their behalf.
mt.route: Compliance scheme, e.g. GreenPak or Green MT
mt.note: Drinks containers are covered by the BCRS deposit system.

nl.summary: Producers placing over 50,000 kg of packaging a year register and pay a waste management contribution to the Afvalfonds.
nl.note: Deposits apply to drinks bottles and cans.

pl.summary: Producers register in the BDO database, report annually and meet recovery targets, usually through a recovery organisation. A wider EPR reform is in progress.
pl.law: Act on Packaging and Packaging Waste Management (2013)
pl.route: Recovery organisation, or pay the product fee
pl.note: Reform proposals would move to a state-led model, with full EPR planned from 2028.

pt.summary: Producers transfer their responsibility to a licensed managing entity and declare the packaging they place on the market.
pt.route: Managing entity, e.g. Sociedade Ponto Verde
pt.note: Registration and reporting run through APA's SILiAmb platform.

ro.summary: Producers must report to the Environment Fund Administration and can transfer their recovery obligations to an authorised PRO (OIREP).
ro.note: A deposit return system (RetuRO) has operated since 2023.

sk.summary: Producers register and usually meet their obligations through a producer responsibility organisation (OZV). Amendments to the system are under discussion.
sk.register: Ministry of the Environment producer register
sk.note: A proposal would let the state Environmental Fund act as a PRO.

si.summary: Producers meet organisational and financial obligations for packaging waste individually or, more commonly, through a licensed scheme.
si.law: Decree on packaging and packaging waste (2021)
si.note: Producers placing under 1,000 kg a year can pay a lump sum.

es.summary: Producers register in the national producer register and meet EPR obligations, now including commercial and industrial packaging, through a collective scheme.
es.route: Collective scheme, e.g. Ecoembes or Ecovidrio
es.note: Spain also has a separate tax on non-reusable plastic packaging.

se.summary: Producers register with the Swedish EPA, report annually and join an approved producer responsibility organisation.
se.law: Ordinance 2022:1274 on producer responsibility for packaging
se.note: Annual reports are due by 31 March.
